designDecisionsAndRationale: D1: replace the Opus join step with a command node rather than inserting a new step, so the route and expected-routes.json stay unchanged and no judgment-free Opus call remains.

D2: the script reproduces the deleted prompt's classification with precedence tracking-rejected > evidence-incomplete > blocked > successful > failed/cancelled/evidence-missing; failed/cancelled stay out of both id lists for reconciliation and selective redispatch.

D3: storage keyed by runtime-owned _rielaInput.workflowExecutionId under scratchRoot tmp, immutable wave-NNN ordinals, fail-closed on unsafe ids or symlinked directories; highest ordinal is the current wave because waves are serial per session.
D4: bounded summary with exact totals, drift-first path ordering and four cap levels; never emits an oversized or silently cut summary.
D5: downstream prompts read the summary instead of the raw join and bind to it by verdict equality.
D6: mock fixtures relabel the wave-outcome model to the script path (plan-push-gate convention) and add partial_success:false to when; payloads and routes unchanged.
D7: the persistent fanoutJoin request variable cannot be removed in-package; operator decided Option A (upstream riela change) on 2026-10-22.
intentionalTradeoffs: Projection is bounded and tested, but riela 0.2.34 still renders the persistent fanoutJoin request variable into later agent prompts until the upstream change ships.

Mock scenarios do not execute the command or render prompts, so live writes under tmp/opus-luna-waves/ and resume-time request-variable reconstruction are not exercised by mocks; the script fails closed.
Wave-1 package-wide checks may fail transiently while sibling plans are mid-edit; wave-release reruns everything on the combined tree.

outOfScopeEdgeCases: Rendered-prompt overflow in later agent steps and next-wave/redispatch branches caused by the persistent request variable (upstream riela, Option A).
More than 999 waves per session (fails closed).

acceptanceCriteria: node-implementation-wave-outcome.json is nodeType command with command.scriptPath scripts/implementation-wave-outcome.py. Its output.jsonSchema is unchanged: the six fields, all required, additionalProperties false.

The script classifies a fanout join deterministically per design D2. It writes fanout-join.json and wave-summary.json into a new immutable tmp/opus-luna-waves/<workflowExecutionId>/wave-NNN/ per design D3, and prints {when:{implementation_blocked,partial_success},payload:<six fields>}.
For a synthetic join of at least 8 MiB, wave-summary.json bytes plus payload bytes are at most 65536. Totals are exact and the per-plan status, blockers and resume criteria are preserved.

Tracking-contract rejections and complete:false waves are blocked with the exact resume criterion 'amend checkpoint: declare artifactRoots / narrow writePaths'. Blocked-only waves report partial_success false.
All ten design test cases pass under unittest with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. No __pycache__ remains in the package.

reconcile-implementations.md no longer tells the agent to read runtimeVariables.fanoutJoin or the joined inbox payload. It locates the current wave summary by the design D3 rule (highest tmp/opus-luna-waves/<own _rielaInput.workflowExecutionId>/wave-NNN/wave-summary.json), requires the summary's workflowExecutionId to match and its verdict to deep-equal the inbox implementation-wave-outcome payload, and treats a mismatch or missing file as a blocking evidence gap.

reconcile-implementations.md takes plans[], dispatchedBranchIds/pendingBranchIds, checkpointProvenance, reviewDecisions, changedFiles, evidencePaths, the changeEvidence aggregates and the selection source-vs-artifact drift paths from the summary. It extracts raw records only by rawPointer with a targeted query, never reads fanout-join.json whole, ignores any raw fanoutJoin in runtimeVariables, and returns waveSummaryPath and rawJoinPath in its payload.

integration-review.md reads the summary at the reconcile-supplied waveSummaryPath, requires it to equal the locator result for its own workflowExecutionId, and uses the summary's dispatchedBranchIds and plans[] instead of native fanoutJoin records, with the same targeted-extraction rule.

All other existing semantics of both prompts are preserved verbatim: checkpoint provenance verification, artifact drift is not a source overwrite, complete:false is a blocking gap, partial_success handling, Luna ownership, the detailed revision handoff, the loopGate contract.
